cards.text: The prophet Isaiah has just told God's people that the Lord GOD of Hosts will cut down the tall trees and clear the forest thickets with an axe (Isaiah 10:33-34). Now he zooms in on one stump, the stump of Jesse, King David's father (Ruth 4:22). Friend, a tree cut down that low isn't a tree anymore, it's a STOOL.

cards.question: Out of the stump of Jesse, what does Isaiah say will spring up?
True or false: Isaiah says the Branch growing from Jesse's roots will wither away.

cards.text: Then Isaiah says the Spirit of the LORD will rest on this Branch, the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, counsel and strength, knowledge and fear of the LORD. Friend, most mornings I'd settle for ONE of those before my first batch.

cards.question: The Spirit of the fear of the LORD will rest on the Branch, and Isaiah says He will ___ in the fear of the LORD.

cards.text: Now Isaiah turns to how this Branch will judge.

cards.question: True or false: the Branch will judge by what His eyes see and decide by what His ears hear.
The Branch won't judge by looks or by what He hears. Isaiah says He will judge the ___ with righteousness.

cards.text: With equity He will decide for the lowly of the earth. Then Isaiah says He will strike the earth.

cards.question: Isaiah says the Branch will strike the earth. What will He strike it with?

answers.text: An iron rod in His hand

cards.text: And He will slay the wicked with the breath of His lips.

cards.question: Isaiah says righteousness will be the belt around the Branch's hips. True or false: faithfulness will be part of what He wears too.

cards.text: Then the picture gets WILD. I mean literally wild, as in animals, starting with a wolf and a lamb.

cards.question: True or false: in Isaiah's picture, the wolf will hunt down the lamb.
The leopard will lie down with the goat, and the calf, the young lion and the fatling will all be together. Who will lead this whole crowd?

cards.text: The cow will graze with the bear, and their young will lie down together. A bear, GRAZING, right next to a cow, like he's never even HEARD of one.

cards.question: Then Isaiah gets to the lion. True or false: in this picture, the lion will eat straw like the ox.

cards.text: The infant will play by the cobra's den, and the toddler will reach into the viper's nest. Friend, I flinch when my oven timer goes off, and this toddler is reaching into a VIPER'S NEST.

cards.question: Isaiah says one thing will not happen anywhere on God's holy mountain. What is it?
Isaiah gives the reason nothing will harm or destroy on God's holy mountain: the earth will be full of the ___ of the ___, as the sea is full of water.

cards.text: Then Isaiah says, "On that day the Root of Jesse will stand as a banner for the peoples." Picture it lifted high, like the OPEN sign I flip on at my bakery every single morning.

cards.question: The Root of Jesse will stand as a banner for the peoples, and the ___ will seek Him.

cards.text: And His place of rest will be glorious. Centuries later, the apostle Paul quotes Isaiah's words about the Root of Jesse while writing about Christ, the One who pulled me out of the dark (Romans 15:8-12).
On that day the Lord will reach out His hand a second time to recover the remnant of His people. The list of places runs from Assyria and Egypt all the way to the islands of the sea.

cards.question: The Lord will raise a banner for the nations and gather the exiles of Israel. And the scattered of Judah? Where will He collect them from?

answers.text: The four corners of the earth
The far side of the Jordan
The plains of Moab near Jericho

cards.text: Then Isaiah turns to Ephraim, the northern kingdom, and Judah, split since the day Ephraim separated from Judah (Isaiah 7:17). They remind me of the dead batteries I shared that drawer with, arguing for YEARS over who had the most charge left.

cards.question: True or false: Isaiah says Ephraim will keep envying Judah.

cards.text: Then Isaiah says Ephraim and Judah will swoop down on the Philistines to the west, and together they will plunder the sons of the east. And the LORD will sweep His hand over the Euphrates with a scorching wind and split it into seven streams.

cards.question: True or false: Isaiah says that after the LORD splits the Euphrates into seven streams, people will cross it with dry sandals.
Isaiah says there will be a highway for the remnant of God's people coming from Assyria. What earlier journey does he compare it to?

answers.text: When Israel came up from Egypt
When Abram set out from Ur

cards.text: Now Isaiah tells his listeners what they will say in that day. It starts, "O LORD, I will praise You."

cards.question: The speaker says the LORD was angry. What has happened to that anger now?
True or false: the speaker says the LORD has brought comfort.

cards.text: Then the speaker says, "Surely God is my salvation…"

cards.question: Because God is the speaker's salvation, what does the speaker decide to do?

cards.text: The speaker goes on: "For the LORD GOD is my strength and my song, and He also has become my salvation." Friend, MY strength is a mustache that can carry three cookie boxes, so this speaker is doing MUCH better than me.
Then Isaiah paints a picture of drawing water from the springs of salvation.

cards.question: In Isaiah's picture, his listeners will draw water from the springs of salvation with ___.

cards.text: And on that day there's more for them to say: "Give praise to the LORD; proclaim His name!"

cards.question: In what they will say on that day, where should the LORD's works be made known?
True or false: these words say the glorious things the LORD has done should be kept quiet.

cards.text: The last line goes out to the citizen of Zion: cry out and sing! Friend, that's my cookie cutter kid Ruby's volume, and when Ruby spoke up, the WHOLE kitchen heard it.

cards.question: True or false: the last line tells the citizen of Zion that the Holy One of Israel is far away from them.
